title: A Blockchain Integrated Hierarchical Attention Graph Model for Cybersecurity and Digital Forensic Investigation
authors: Amani Aljehani; Syed Hamid Hasan; Usman Ali Khan
abstract: In recent years, blockchain-based attacks and cybersecurity incidents have continued to evolve in scale and become more complicated. Various prior forensic models suffer from limited multimodal fusion and weak analytical depth. This paper proposes a novel Hierarchical Attention Graph Augmented Forensic Network for secure forensic investigation. The proposed model combines a hierarchical graph attention network with blockchain to capture latent anomaly patterns. The methodology begins by collecting large-scale data, followed by structured data pre-processing, blockchain hashing process, as well as graph construction that links metadata, events, and entities. The developed model incorporates three significant mechanisms: (i) multilevel feature attention, (ii) encoding temporal sequence, and (iii) aggregating cross graphs to generate a unified latent model. A softmax layer classifies the attributes via entity space projection. The experimental analysis is carried out by comparing the developed model with prior models to determine the effectiveness of a secure forensic framework. The proposed model attained an accuracy of 98.96%, a precision of 98.84%, a recall of 98.72%, an F1-score of 98.77%, and a specificity of 98.76%.

title: Emoji use as a self-branding strategy in male and female Arab influencers’ Instagram bios: a corpus linguistic study
authors: Manal Alangari; Alyaa Olwi
abstract: This study explores the use of emojis in Instagram bios as a self-branding strategy among male and female social media influencers. The study examined two corpora comprising 2,184 bios in total, equally split between male and female (1,092 each). The analysis classified the emojis most frequently used in the two gendered corpora according to their categories and functions using corpus-assisted tools. The results confirmed the use of emojis as a valid element in bios to serve multiple purposes. Female influencers emphasized their femininity in their choice of emojis under certain categories, such as Animal & Nature [Cartoon-style illustration of a pink five-petal flower with a yellow center, a single green leaf, and a curved black stem outlined in bold lines], whereas male influencers emphasized power in their use of emojis under the category of People & Body [Yellow cartoon-style hand icon with an extended index finger pointing downward, outlined in black, against a white background]. While most emoji sequences in the female corpus presented the combined function of Concept and Stance, the most prominent function of emoji sequences in the male corpus was Concept and Action. The study shows that emojis and emoji sequences play an important role as a self-branding strategy in influencers’ bios in a creative and interesting manner.

title: Mathematical modeling of explainable AI based false data injection attack detection for resilient artificial intelligence of things
authors: Mohammed A. AlAqil; Hend Khalid Alkahtani; Nasser Allheeib; Jahangir Khan; Hanadi Alkhudhayr; Sami M. Alenezi; Malak Bakheet Alharbi; Sultan Almutairi
abstract: The artificial intelligence of things (AIoT) comprises the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies and the internet of things (IoT) infrastructure. The main aim of the AIoT is to design highly effective IoT operation, enhance human-machine interaction, and improve data analytics and data management. In the AIoT system, the AI is embedded into the infrastructure elements, namely programs and chipsets, which are interlinked via the IoT network. Cybersecurity in the AIoT employs AI technologies, particularly machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), and neural networks to defend connected IoT devices, networks, and data from recent cyber threats. Since IoT devices have restricted capability, storage, and power, the AI offers intelligent and effective defenses that can learn to identify anomalies in real time. Therefore, we present a mathematically guided and explainable AI-based framework titled the mutual information-based feature ranking for detecting false data injection attacks (MIFR-DFDIA) approach in resilient distributed cybersecurity networks. The MIFR-DFDIA aims to enhance cybersecurity resilience by accurately identifying and mitigating false data injection attacks that compromise data integrity. Initially, data preprocessing was performed to handle outliers, missing values, and feature standardization for ensuring high-quality input data for analysis. Mutual information was then utilized for optimal feature selection to identify the most informative attributes effectively. For classification, a hybrid model such as a stacked variational autoencoder and a wasserstein generative adversarial network was deployed for robust and precise recognition of false data injection attacks in cybersecurity distributed systems. Finally, the explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) method based SHAP was incorporated to interpret model predictions and improve transparency in decision-making. The experimental result analysis of the MIFR-DFDIA method was carried out for a benchmark dataset, and the comparative analysis exhibited the improved solution over other techniques concerning various metrics.

title: Data-Centric Dataset Characterization for Tabular Learning Using Uniqueness Domains Knowledge Profiling
authors: Khaled Bahnasy; Mohamed Hamdy; Doaa Hegazy; Mohamed Dahab
abstract: While dataset learning complexity has traditionally been measured using statistical meta-features or by the predictive ability of an empirical model, the volume of explicitly defined, deterministic knowledge inside a dataset has usually remained unmeasured. In this paper, a knowledge-based method is presented to evaluate dataset learning complexity using the Uniqueness Domain, defined as the set of all$\mathbf{1 0 0 \%}$accurate class association rules of the dataset. The UniqAR algorithm is used to extract the uniqueness domains of twelve tabular datasets [1]. Three knowledge-volume metrics are introduced: Absolute Knowledge Volume$(A K V)$, Case-Normalized Knowledge Volume ($C K V$), and Feature-Value-Normalized Knowledge Volume$(F K V)$. In addition, a composite index, the Knowledge Challenge Index$(K C I)$, is proposed to relate extraction effort to extracted deterministic knowledge. It is shown that the number of deterministic symbolic patterns per unit information can vary by up to four orders of magnitude across datasets, and that the size of the uniqueness domain is driven mainly by feature-value diversity, rather than by the number of rows. Based on these observations, a dataset “Complexity Profile” is constructed, which can distinguish datasets that are transparent with respect to their logical structures from datasets that are relatively opaque.

title: Developing a Computer-Aided Diagnosis System for Breast Cancer Detection
authors: Abdulaziz M. Alomran; Eyad T. Attar; Ahmad A. Jiman
abstract: Computer-Aided Diagnosis (CAD) is utilized for the detection and diagnosis of abnormal tumors, including breast cancer, a significant health concern for women, particularly in developing countries like Saudi Arabia. With breast cancer ranking as the second most prevalent cancer globally and the most common in Saudi Arabia, early detection through mammography is critical for effective treatment. The Breast Imaging-Reporting and Data System (BI-RADS) classifies breast cancer stages to inform treatment plans. Researchers are focused on developing CAD systems employing deep learning and conventional machine learning for enhanced mammogram analysis. Despite the high accuracy of conventional methods, challenges remain in handling large datasets. This research aims to develop a CAD system that enhances breast cancer detection through mammogram images. This research utilized a dataset of breast cancer cases from King Abdulaziz University's Sheikh Mohammed Hussein Al-Amoudi Center of Excellence. The dataset was categorized using the BIRADS system and was used to train, validate, and test a classification network for various breast cancer images, incorporating 248 randomly selected images. The analysis process included image preprocessing, where RGB images were converted to grayscale, noise was reduced using Gaussian filters, and contrast was enhanced. Otsu's threshold method facilitated image segmentation, with morphological operators applied to refine the region of interest. For classification, texture and shape features were extracted, analyzed, and selected using ANOVA1-test. The classification was conducted using Artificial Neural Networks (ANN). This developed CAD system utilizing an ANN classifier to assist doctors in detecting breast cancer, achieving 96.0% accuracy.

title: Validity of Synthetic Tabular Data Using Rules and Uniqueness Domains
authors: Mohamed Hamdy; Khaled Bahnasy; Mohamed Dahab; Doaa Hegazy
abstract: Evaluation of synthetic data generation usually focuses on statistical similarity and utility. It neglects semantic and logical constraints of real domains. This paper introduces a rule based method for assessing the validity of synthetic tabular data. Using of class-based unique rules to define a uniqueness domain for a dataset is introduced. These domains serve as explicit knowledge landmark which synthetic data should reach for validation. Ten real datasets using sampling, interpolation-based methods, and deep learning models have been tested. This paper focuses on two important things: pseudo-validity and true validity. The results show a big gap between them both. A lot of generators make data that looks good but is not really valid. Synthetic samples frequently do not possess the distinguishing logical attributes of their designated class. All generators failed on a high cardinality dataset with a huge uniqueness domains because the absence of using uniqueness domains which can lead to generate synthetic data that is semantically consistent in future hybrid AI systems.

title: A Survey of Neuro-Symbolic AI: Integration Paradigms, Taxonomy, and Formal Specification
authors: Mohamed Hamdy; Khaled Bahnasy; Mohamed Dahab; Doaa Hegazy
abstract: Explainable AI is not feasible by applying most the common methods of low-level deep perception models. Deep learning (DL) excels at picking out patterns, but let's be real: it is a total data hog, it's impossible to see inside of it, and it usually lacks even basic logic. It has a lack of reasoning abilities. Symbolic systems using different Knowledge representation like Knowledge Graphs (KG) and rules can provide a good complement option towards hybrid AI systems that can provide explainable AI. The integration of low-level data deriven deepl learning and symbolic systems can shape a path to realize future hybrid AI systems. This paper introduce a survey that introduce a taxonomy and shows a systematic review on the different synergistic integration approaches.

title: Enhanced Sentiment Analysis Toward Specific Locations and Neighborhoods with Advanced Machine Learning Techniques
authors: Nahla Aljojo; Noor Bagazi; Maha Alshehri; Somaiyah Al-Shabeer; Haneen Alzahrani; Ahmed Alamri; Areej ALSHUTAYRI; Aisha Blfgeh; Iqbal ALSALEH; Ammar Almutawa; Alaa Alsaig
abstract: Sentiment analysis has become an important field of study in recent years because it enables the evaluation of public opinions collected from multiple data sources. This study highlights the importance of understanding public perceptions regarding specific areas and communities, which is essential for urban planning, tourism, real estate, and community engagement. By using diverse sources such as social media platforms and online reviews, the study applies sentiment analysis techniques to identify shared attitudes and emotional reactions toward geographical locations. The resulting analysis provides detailed insights that support decision-making processes in areas such as city planning, tourism development, and public service improvement. These sentiments are classified into three categories: positive, negative, and neutral. This study applies comparative machine learning approaches to a QA-based geospatial aspect-based sentiment analysis (ABSA) dataset in order to examine probabilistic and sequential modeling behavior. The research specifically focuses on four major characteristics: “price,” “safety,” “transit-location,” and “general,” which were identified as the most common aspects within the dataset. The methodology involved dividing the dataset, containing both single and multiple place mentions, into train, development (dev), and test sets. Specifically, 70% of the data was allocated for training, 10% for development, and 20% for testing. The evaluated models included logistic regression, gradient boosting, Bayesian network, long short-term memory, and GRU. Among all models, the Bayesian network achieved the highest accuracy of 88%, demonstrating strong potential for urban sentiment analysis and informed decision-making in city planning and tourism
journal: Journal of Artificial Intelligence and Technology

title: Redesigning the Process of Hospital Discharge by the Integration of AI Predictive Modeling
authors: Salma Elhag; Renad Alshamrani; Layan Althobaiti
abstract: Hospital readmission is a major indicator of the success and service quality of healthcare facilities. High readmission rates is a common issue globally, as it indicates poor quality of services leading to high financial costs. Studies focus on finding solutions to reduce readmission rates including AI predictive modeling. Traditional hospital discharge process relies only on human assessment without utilizing these models, which limit the early detection of high-risk cases leading to patient treatment delays, applying costs upon unexpected readmission. This research aims to redesign hospital discharge process by integrating the predictive model for diabetic patient's readmission into hospital systems, to reduce readmission rates, cut financial costs, enable healthcare providers to develop customized post discharge care plan according to patient case risk to improve quality of services. The simulation results using Bizagi Modeler shows that the redesigned process achieved 17.82% reduction in readmission rates, 38% reduction in processing time, with nearly 100% detection accuracy in defining high risk patients. These results demonstrate that the redesigned process supports medical decision making, reduce the workload, improve resources utilization, and cut financial costs associated with unexpected readmissions.

title: A Comparative Review of Liveness Detection Methods for Hand Vein Identification
authors: Asma Bahumayd; Sumaya Mustafa; Sumaiyah Aldhahri; Rania A. Elmanfaloty
abstract: Hand vein identification is a biometric technique that recognizes individuals using the unique vascular patterns beneath the skin captured by near infrared imaging. Although it provides high security, it remains vulnerable to presentation attacks such as printed images, artificial hands, and replayed infrared data, making liveness detection a necessary security component as well as a practical system-level consideration. This study aims to identify the most effective liveness detection approaches by systematically reviewing and comparing reported results from prior studies. The comparison is conducted using performance metrics reported in the literature, including accuracy, error rates, and processing time, in addition to practical system considerations. Furthermore, a user questionnaire is analyzed to assess user preference and acceptance, providing insight into the trade-off between security and usability.

title: Benchmarking Reference-Free LLM Agent Robustness Under Schema, Policy, and Toolset Drift
authors: Mohammad Hasbi Assidiqi; Daniyal Alghazzawi; Suaad Alarifi; Li Cheng
abstract: Tool-using large language model (LLM) agents fail when external interfaces evolve, yet most evaluations emphasize static competence rather than adaptation under drift. We studied this problem with controlled schema, policy, and toolset perturbations derived from tau2-bench retail tasks and distinguished between a reference-guided replay benchmark and reference-free adaptation. In a reference-guided exact-trajectory setting, GPT-4o mini reached 0.708 task success over 216 trials, establishing that the benchmark contains recoverable structure. We then evaluated five OpenRouter-served models—GPT-4o mini, GPT-4o, Kimi K2, DeepSeek V3, and Qwen3-32B—under a reference-free protocol scoring end-state task completion across 270 trials per model-condition cell (30 scenarios × 3 episodes × 3 drift families). Static baselines range from 0.130 to 0.432 across models. Blind replay consistently degrades reference-free task success relative to static for four of five models; Kimi K2 is the exception, for which both blind replay and rules-only significantly improve over the static baseline. Rules-only shows model-dependent effects, significantly improving for Kimi K2 and Qwen3-32B while showing no significant difference for the remaining three models. A normalization-ablation condition confirms that the drift-inversion layer is load-bearing for toolset drift; schema-obedience determines whether this layer is effective.Within the three evaluated drift types and controller conditions, the reference-guided replay advantage does not transfer to reference-free task success, and the primary barriers are hidden-state reconstruction and branch selection across multiple candidate orders and products.

title: Smartphone Authentication Using Face ID with Mask
authors: Njoud Majed Alharbi; Awny Sayed
abstract: Face recognition has become a key technology for user authentication in modern smartphones. However, the widespread use of face masks during the COVID-19 outbreak has posed significant challenges due to facial occlusion. To address this issue, this paper proposes a hybrid face recognition framework that integrates deep learning embeddings with handcrafted texture descriptors to improve robustness under masked face conditions. Four hybrid configurations are evaluated by combining FaceNet or MobileNetV2 with either Local Binary Patterns (LBP) or Gabor wavelets. Experiments evaluate identity recognition performance under masked, unmasked, and mixed scenarios using both the Real-World Masked Face Dataset (RMFRD) and the proposed Real-World Masked and Unmasked Face Dataset (RWMUF). Notably, the FaceNet with LBP approach achieves high recognition accuracies of$98.63 \%, 99.21 \%$, and 99.14 % for masked, unmasked, and mixed faces, respectively, on the RWMUF dataset, and$96.81 \%, 98.81 \%$, and 96.48 % on RMFRD, clearly outperforming other configurations, and is integrated into a mobile application for real-time face recognition. These results highlight the effectiveness of combining deep learning embeddings with handcrafted features for robust masked face recognition. The RWMUF dataset is available at: https://github.com/NjoudAl-harbi/A-Real-World-Masked-and-Unmasked-Face-Dataset-RWMUF-Dataset-

title: Transformer Model for Direct Translation of Spoken Text to Arabic Sign Language (ArSL)
authors: Samah Abbas; Dimah Alahmadi; Hassanin Al-Barhamtoshy
abstract: Arabic Sign Language (ArSL) is a formal language used by Deaf and Hard of Hearing communities. It helps them understand Arabic spoken by hearing people, particularly in formal speech, such as news or sermons. The production of sign language systems can support communication by translating spoken languages into ArSL videos. However, current systems often fail to meet user needs due to poor translation of grammatical structures and limited ability to capture the textual meaning of speech. This research focused on a neural machine translation (NMT) approach to convert spoken Arabic texts into Arabic Sign Language (ArSL) using a transformer-based model to overcome these difficulties. The ArSL video of the sign is produced as a series of 2D skeletal poses. The proposed methodology is based on an encoder-decoder architecture: texts are represented by a transformer model, and a posture decoder generates gestures. The model is evaluated using quantitative criteria, such as mean square error (MSE) and the dynamic time warping (DTW) measure, as well as qualitative evaluations by sign language experts and users from the Deaf and Hard of Hearing community. The study uses Friday sermon data as a reference to build the translation model and applies optimization techniques such as temporal modulation, noise addition, and resizing to enhance performance. The results show that the enhanced model improves the quality of gesture representation, reducing DTW by 43.4% relative to the baseline in the non-continuous ArSL test. On the other hand, in the Continuous ArSL test using Short Sermon, the DTW is reduced by around 2.25%. In addition, the enhanced model received high user acceptance, with 75.2% satisfaction. Moreover, unified qualitative evaluation criteria for sign language production are proposed, including clarity, accuracy, consistency, and naturalness, which could serve as a basis for future evaluations in this field. These criteria are used to evaluate the generated ArSL and measure user satisfaction.
journal: ACM Transactions on Asian and Low-Resource Language Information Processing

title: Assessing the Use of Synthetic Tabular Data: An Analysis of the Adult Dataset
authors: Abdullah Balamash
abstract: In this study, we evaluate the effectiveness of synthetic data generated using the Gaussian Copula (GC) and Conditional Tabular Generative Adversarial Network (CTGAN) models within the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) framework by applying it to the Adult data set [1]. This is done in three steps:(1) Training and Testing on Real Data (Baseline), (2) Training on Synthetic Data and Testing on Real Data (TSTR), (3) Training on (Synthetic + Real Data) and Testing on Real Data (Augmentation with Real Data), (4) Minority Class Oversampling. The TSTR results show that synthetic data preserves the predictive features of baseline data. Augmentation with real data does not improve the performance when there is enough real data. When we have a class-imbalance scenario, synthetic minority oversampling improves the recall for the minority class (e.g., from 0.60 to 0.80 with CTGAN) at the expense of the precision in a way that underperforms traditional techniques such as random oversampling and class weighting. Overall, our findings suggest that synthetic data can be used when we do not have enough data, but it is not good enough to address class imbalance.
journal: Journal of King Abdulaziz University-Engineering Sciences

title: A Comparative Study of Ore Reserve Estimation Methods: Traditional Triangulation vs. Geovia Surpac & Maptek Vulcan at the Al Khabra Phosphate Deposit, Saudi Arabia
authors: Hussein A. Saleem; Mostafa A-B Ebrahim; Gamal S. Abdelhaffez; Abdul Majeed Al Aenezi
abstract: Ore reserve estimation drives mining's economic viability. Reserve estimation in mining involves determining the amount of economically extractable minerals in a given deposit. This study, using 63 boreholes, conducts a comparison of triangulation, Geovia Surpac, and Maptek Vulcan for Al Khabra's phosphate reserves, Saudi Arabia. It computes grade, volume, and tonnage, revealing a 2.05% difference in Surpac and 0.68% in Vulcan. Specifically, the traditional triangulation method yielded a reserve of 278.6 million tonnes (Mt) at an average grade of 21.75% P2O5. In comparison, Geovia Surpac estimated 284.3 Mt, and Maptek Vulcan estimated 280.5 Mt at a grade of 22.25% P2O5. The findings highlight method synergy, optimizing phosphate mine planning and ore recovery for long-term profitability.
journal: Journal of King Abdulaziz University-Engineering Sciences

title: A Robust Tamper-Resistant and Location-Aware Authentication Protocol for Securing Charging Services in V2G Environments
authors: Muhammad Umer; Muhammad Farooq; Syed Asad Ali Naqvi; Khalid Mahmood; Bander Alzahrani; Ashok Kumar Das; Shehzad Ashraf Chaudhry
abstract: The rapid increase in electric vehicles (EVs) and the widespread deployment of charging stations have made secure authentication a critical requirement in Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) environments. The growing interconnection among EVs, charging stations, and grid infrastructure introduces serious security and privacy challenges, including impersonation, replay, ephemeral secret leakage, and physical tampering attacks. Although several authentication protocols have been proposed for EV charging services, many existing schemes lack robust tamper-resistant and location-aware authentication capabilities and remain unsuitable for dynamic and resource-constrained V2G conditions. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a robust, tamper-resistant, and location-sensitive authentication protocol for securing EV charging services in V2G environments. The proposed protocol integrates configurable Arbiter Physical Unclonable Functions (A-PUFs) to provide device-level protection against physical tampering and unauthorized charging access. It also employs lightweight cryptographic primitives and techniques, including one-way hash functions, XOR operations, concatenation operations, and timestamp-based freshness verification, to support efficient mutual authentication and secure session key agreement. The security of the proposed protocol is evaluated through informal analysis and formal verification under the Random Oracle Model (ROM). Furthermore, comparative analysis demonstrates that the proposed protocol achieves a 17.16% reduction in communication cost and a 7.49% reduction in average computation cost compared with existing authentication protocols while maintaining strong security features. The results confirm that the proposed scheme enhances the security, efficiency, and practical deployability of EV charging authentication for next-generation V2G networks.

title: Deep Learning-Based Phishing URL Detection Using Deep Neural Network and Convolutional Neural Networks
authors: Ahmed Bahurmuz
abstract: Phishing attacks remain one of the most significant cybersecurity threats, where malicious websites attempt to deceive users into revealing sensitive information such as login credentials and financial data. Traditional phishing detection techniques often struggle to identify newly generated phishing websites due to the rapidly evolving tactics used by attackers. This study proposes a deep learning-based approach for phishing URL detection by comparing the performance of two neural network architectures, namely a Deep Neural Network (DNN) and a one-dimensional Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). The experiments were conducted using a phishing URL dataset containing structural and behavioral features extracted from website and URL characteristics. Data preprocessing was performed by removing irrelevant identifiers, eliminating duplicate samples, and applying feature normalization to improve model training stability. The dataset was divided into training, validation, and testing subsets using stratified sampling to preserve the class distribution. Both models were evaluated using multiple performance metrics including accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve. The experimental results show that the CNN model achieved superior performance with an accuracy of 93.2 percent and an AUC value of 0.988, outperforming the DNN model across all evaluation metrics. These findings demonstrate that convolutional neural networks are more effective in capturing complex feature interactions within phishing URL datasets and can provide a reliable approach for automated phishing detection systems in cybersecurity applications.

title: Sentiment and Emotion Analysis of Public Discourse on ChatGPT Using VADER Sentiment Analysis
authors: Ibrahiem M. M. El Emary
abstract: The rapid emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies has ignited global discussions, particularly around ChatGPT, an AI tool designed to transform how humans interact with digital systems. This study explores public sentiment and emotional reactions towards ChatGPT during its initial launch period, analyzing a dataset of tweets sourced from Kaggle. Leveraging the VADER sentiment analysis algorithm, the research categorizes user reactions into positive, negative, and neutral sentiments, while also identifying key emotional tones such as joy, fear, and skepticism. The findings reveal that positive sentiment prevailed, reflecting excitement about ChatGPT’s innovative capabilities, while concerns regarding ethics and job displacement gradually surfaced, underscoring the dual nature of public opinion. Through visualizations such as bar charts, time-based sentiment trends, and word clouds, the study highlights the dynamic engagement of users with ChatGPT and its broader implications for society. Key insights suggest that public perceptions of AI are influenced by its perceived utility, accessibility, and ethical considerations. While the study demonstrates the efficacy of VADER in capturing sentiment trends, it also acknowledges limitations, including the inability to detect sarcasm or nuanced emotional expressions. The implications of this research extend to AI developers, policymakers, and researchers, emphasizing the importance of public engagement strategies that address ethical concerns and build trust. Additionally, the study contributes to the growing body of knowledge on digital society, offering a framework for understanding how emerging technologies shape public discourse. Future research could focus on comparative analyses across different social media platforms or delve deeper into the evolution of public sentiment over time. By unraveling these complexities, this study aims to guide the responsible development and deployment of AI technologies in an increasingly interconnected world.

title: Harnessing Artificial Intelligence in universities
authors: Komal Khalid; Juri Alsini
abstract: This research examines the complex relationships between artificial intelligence learning motivation (AILM), intention (AILI), efficacy (AILE), and student creativity (SC) among Saudi Arabian undergraduate and graduate students. A quantitative approach was employed, gathering data from bilingual questionnaires administered to 466 students across five Saudi universities, utilizing validated scales for AILM (intrinsic/extrinsic), AILI, AILE, and SC. Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) was utilized to access direct and indirect effects. The analysis established the nine hypotheses, signifying that AILM significantly influences AILI and AILE, thus, enhances SC. AILE and AILI could act as mediators between AILM and SC, whereas the serial mediation path (AILM→AILI→AILE→SC) represents the highest mediator. The research implies the importance for Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030-compliant education reforms that promote both intrinsic and extrinsic motivation (ILM and ELM), intention reciprocated into learning behavior, and the development of AILE to enhance SC.
journal: IJERI International Journal of Educational Research and Innovation

title: Profiling Cross-Border Remote Cybersecurity Employment for Jurisdictional Complexity via Unsupervised Role-Arrangement Clustering
authors: Ahmed Saeed Bahurmuz
abstract: Cross-border remote work has expanded the practical footprint of cybersecurity labor beyond traditional organizational and national boundaries, raising jurisdictional questions about employment governance, taxation, and cross-border data access. However, empirical cyberlaw research is often limited by the availability of legal outcome variables at scale. This study presents a dataset-only, unsupervised method to detect and summarize cross-border remote work configurations that plausibly differ in jurisdictional coordination burden. Using a structured salary dataset of cybersecurity-related roles, we operationalize cross-border status as a mismatch between employee residence and company location. To avoid a trivial domesticversus-cross-border split, clustering is performed exclusively on cross-border records. Mixed categorical and numeric features—remote-work intensity, employment type, experience level, company size, and optional role grouping and jurisdiction categories—are represented via Gower distance. We apply averagelinkage hierarchical clustering to the resulting precomputed distance matrix and select a solution using silhouette score. To prevent unstable singleton patterns from being reported as typologies, we enforce a minimum cluster size (n≥5) by merging microclusters into the nearest larger cluster using mean inter-cluster Gower distance. The final cross-border typology yields two interpretable groups: a dominant “enterprise remote-first” configuration (n=52) with high fully remote prevalence and strong concentration in large firms, and a smaller “mid/small mixed-remote” configuration (n=6) with no large-firm representation and a tighter salary distribution. The dominant group spans many distinct residence→company corridors, suggesting broader crossjurisdiction exposure and coordination needs, while the smaller group reflects more constrained organizational settings. The study contributes an interpretable clustering workflow with explicit micro-cluster handling for exploratory cyberlaw analyses, and it delineates the limits of inference when legal compliance variables are absent.

title: Enhancing Open Access to Data Science Education: Analyzing Skill Patterns Using LDA and K-Means Clustering in the Learning Path Index Dataset
authors: Ibrahiem M. M. El Emary
abstract: This study examines the application of Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) and K-Means clustering techniques to analyze the Learning Path Index Dataset, with the aim of identifying and categorizing data science education skills. By employing these machine learning models, the research reveals distinct skill patterns and clusters that characterize the dataset, highlighting prevalent skills and potential gaps in data science education accessible through open educational resources (OER). The findings demonstrate specific clusters of beginner to advanced data science topics, offering insights into the accessibility and distribution of educational content. These results can guide educators and platform developers in enhancing the structure and delivery of data science education, thereby improving learner outcomes and resource allocation. The study also discusses the broader implications for educational strategy and policy, emphasizing the role of targeted analytics in optimizing educational offerings in an increasingly digital landscape. Future research directions include expanding the dataset and applying similar analytical frameworks to other fields within open education to further validate and refine these findings.

title: An Intelligent Health Guide Based on AI and Metaverse to Enhance Prevention and Quality of Life
authors: Abdullah Basahel; Adnan Ahmed Abi Sen; Abdulrahman Abdullah Basahel; Nour Mahmoud Bahbouh; Mohammed Abdullah Basahel; Layan Mohammed Albejawi
abstract: The health sector is considered one of the main pillars in improving the quality of life and building sustainable and livable cities, given its direct connection with several other vital sectors such as transportation, environment, and crowd management. Recent studies indicate that investing in prevention and health awareness is one of the most effective ways to reduce medical costs and enhance community capacity for facing pandemics and chronic diseases. In this research, we propose a multi-layered health framework based on artificial intelligence and the metaverse, aiming to create an intelligent virtual health guide that works as your daily virtual companion. The proposed framework relies on an advanced medical knowledge base to provide continuous and personalized health instructions, as well as realistic interaction with the user in a virtual environment. The framework also employs Agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies for intelligent decision-making in emergency situations, in addition to early detection of disease indicators and enhancing health literacy. In order to improve the quality of life and lessen the strain on health systems, the suggested framework aims to replace the conventional treatment-based healthcare model with a proactive preventive model that depends on ongoing monitoring and early intervention. It also guides users to appropriate emergency procedures or communication with specialized medical authorities. This stage is considered the primary design phase, focusing on building and recommending after disease occurrence, and can be supported by a set of health applications and uses in real environments. The proposed framework has not yet been fully implemented as a system; future work will focus on developing an applied model and evaluating it in real environments.

title: Agentic AI in Distributed SDN: Synchronization and Design Framework
authors: Rawan Alsheikh; Etimad Fadel; Nadine Akkari
abstract: Large-scale Software-Defined Networking (SDN) deployments are increasingly adopting Physically Distributed but Logically Centralized (PDLC) control planes, in which multiple controllers must coordinate to maintain a consistent global view of the network. In practice, this creates a persistent trade-off between state consistency and synchronization overhead under limited control-plane budgets. Existing AI-based synchronization solutions often rely on centralized learning and decision components, which can reduce scalability and introduce single-point-of-failure-like dependence. This paper presents a design framework for adaptive synchronization in PDLC SDN from an agentic AI perspective. The objective is to express synchronization as a budget-aware decision process that can be learned by controller-resident agents while enabling cooperative learning without centralized run-time action selection. We model synchronization as a budget-aware Markov Decision Process (MDP) with explicit state, action, and reward definitions that capture staleness, constrained neighbor selection, and benefit-cost tradeoffs. Based on this formulation, we adopt Centralized Training and Decentralized Execution (CTDE): decentralized Actors make local synchronization decisions at run time, while a trainingtime Critic provides coordination signals to stabilize multi-agent learning. The framework is instantiated with Communication Multi-Agent Actor-Critic (C-MAAC) and extended with an Attention-Based Critic (ABC-MAAC), where attention suppresses low-impact inter-controller relations and emphasizes influential ones before value estimation. Complexity verification shows linear per-update scaling for C-MAAC and an additional quadratic interaction term for ABC-MAAC due to pairwise attention, while preserving decentralized, budget-aware run-time execution.

title: Efficient convergence of the D.A. algorithm: stability visuals and practical applications
authors: Aftab Hussain; Danish Ali; Amer Hassan Albargi
abstract: In this paper, we introduce an iterative procedure for approximating fixed points of a contraction mapping. We also discuss its stability under mild conditions. By exploring the properties related to uniformly convex Banach spaces, we can establish a collection of convergence outcomes, both weak and strong, about generalized nonexpansive mappings. Numerical examples demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms several existing iterative schemes. We validate our main result by applying it to find an approximate solution of a fractional Volterra-Fredholm integro-differential equation. The findings extend the scope of numerous previously published results.
journal: Journal of Mathematics and Computer Science

title: Approximation of Fixed Points for E-Type Enriched Nonexpansive Mappings with Applications
authors: Mujahid Abbas; Ahad Hamoud Alotaibi; Muhammad Waseem Asghar
abstract: In this research, we propose an inertial-type iterative scheme constructed by an E-type enriched nonexpansive mappings in the framework of uniformly convex Banach spaces. Strong and weak convergence results along with stability result for the proposed algorithm are presented. Numerical examples and comparisons with well known existing iterative schemes with the help of graphs are presented to demonstrate the efficiency of our proposed scheme. It is shown that the algorithm presented herein converges more faster to fixed point and competitive on the examples considered for this class of mappings. As applications, we apply the scheme to solve variational inequality problems, constrained optimization problems, and split feasibility problems. Moreover, we use the proposed approach to solve a functional differential equation.

title: Federated Learning and Zero Trust Framework for Anomaly Detection in Distributed IIoT-Cloud Systems
authors: Fadi Bata; Mahmoud Aljawarneh; Qais Al-Na’amneh; Rahaf Hazaymih; Ahmad Saleh Alhazaimeh
abstract: The convergence of Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) and hybrid clouds creates data-rich ecosystems but introduces severe security vulnerabilities, especially from insider threats who can bypass traditional defenses. This challenge is amplified in distributed IIoT settings where compromised components act as insiders. This paper proposes a novel framework synergizing Federated Learning (FL) for privacy-preserving, decentralized anomaly detection with a Zero Trust (ZT) architecture for robust security. Using the HAI dataset, our simulations show FL models achieve high discriminative power (AUC > 0.95) but struggle with precision, leading to volatile F1-scores. We critically analyze the framework's resilience to attacks, finding that while ZT provides a secure operational foundation, more intelligent ZT mechanisms are needed to actively filter content-based model attacks, a key direction for future work.

authors: Abdulrhman Alorini; Suleiman Abahussein; Abdullah Bin Sawad; Indra Mckie; Mohammed Althubyani; Afnan Bukhari; Noura Abdi; Kiran Ijaz; Mukesh Prasad; A. Baki Kocaballi

title: SWOT-TOE framework to alleviate quality assurance in machine learning software system: human-agentic AI approaches
authors: Sarra Ayouni; Rafiq Ahmad Khan; Hathal Salamah Alwageed; Ismail Keshta; Alaa Omran Almagrabi; Musaad Alzahrani
abstract: Background The increased use of Machine Learning (ML) systems has posed critical Quality Assurance (QA) issues in areas of security, privacy and performance. Despite advances, QA frameworks for ML remain disjointed. The work examines QA through the Technological, Organizational, and Environmental (TOE) model and proposes human-agentic AI actions to enhance assurance mechanisms. This paper aims to identify, compare and model QA problems in ML software systems and recommend a SWOT-TOE (Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, and Threats) matrix to enhance human-agentic AI-based QA problems. Methodology The study uses a mixed-method design, which includes systematic literature review (SLR), a quantitative survey, and comparative data modelling. QA issues are coded using the TOE structure and the association tests are linear-by-linear tests to investigate the relationship between the literature and survey results. A SWOT-TOE matrix and mathematical modelling are used to assess key QA issues and to solve them. Results The analysis shows that most of the QA problems revolve around interpretability of models, integrity of data, organizational readiness and regulatory limits. The linear-by-linear association results suggest that there is a strong correlation of the patterns of QA that are identified by the literature and those documented in the survey. Comparative data modeling shows the differences in priorities of QA between the regions. The suggested SWOT-TOE framework combines human-agentic solutions (e.g., adaptive auditing and explainable AI) to enhance QA and security. Conclusion The combination of the TOE framework and human-agentic AI practices and quantitative models allows a systematic approach to solving complex QA problems in ML systems. The research leads to the creation of human-centered, adaptive QA strategies, which foster trust, transparency, and sustainability in AI-powered settings. The framework assists developers, QA engineers, and policymakers to increase security, reliability, and accountability in ML ecosystems.

title: A bio-inspired neuromorphic framework for decentralized fault detection and renewable optimization in smart grids
authors: Mohammad Barr; Tawfeeq Shawly; Ahmed A. Alsheikhy; Yahia Said; Shaaban M. Shaaban; Aws AbuEid
abstract: Modern smart grids encounter several challenges, including the variability of renewable energy sources with power fluctuations of ±35% in solar farms across the Arabian Gulf countries, delays in centralized control, with latencies of 150–200 ms, including all time needed from sending data to receiving control commands, and increased susceptibility to cyber threats, with a 30% annual increase in grid intrusions. Incorporating renewable energy into smart grids presents significant challenges, including intermittent generation, characterized by ±30% solar volatility, slow fault detection, and response times exceeding 500 ms in traditional systems, as well as centralized system weaknesses. This paper presents SwarmNet-5G, a bio-inspired neural network that integrates stigmergic learning and spiking neural networks (SNNs) for decentralized grid management to resolve existing issues. It merges Internet of Things (IoT)-edge intelligence, spiking neuromorphic computing, and swarm-based stigmergy to enable grid optimization. Its design decreases latency by 40% compared to typical deep reinforcement learning (DRL). It achieves a fault detection accuracy of 99.62% within 8.17 ms and requires 50 ms for repair, aligning with Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 goal of achieving 50% renewable energy. Simulation results performed on the IEEE 39-bus using a dataset show that the solution allocated power during peak demand, such as a 20% load increase, with an efficiency of 92%, while typical DRL reached 78%. Additionally, the model projected annual savings of.2B in maintenance costs and a reduction of 4.8 megatons in CO2 emissions per year.

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE DRIVEN FACIAL TRACKING AND PRIVACY IN METAVERSE PSYCHIATRY: TECHNICAL FOUNDATIONS AND CLINICAL POTENTIAL OF THE META QUEST PRO
authors: Bayan Turki Bagasi
abstract: The metaverse is rapidly transforming healthcare delivery, especially into psychiatric evaluation and treatment. Among head-mounted displays (HMDs), the Meta Quest Pro distinguishes itself with its built-in artificial intelligence (AI) accelerators and integrated machine learning models that enable real-time facial tracking. These innovations address key metaverse-based mental health care challenges by enhancing emotional realism, patient engagement, and clinical utility. This article discusses the technological foundations required for emotionally responsive avatars and on-device inference, which are critical for preserving privacy in sensitive clinical environments. By evaluating Meta Quest Pro's capabilities, this study positions it as a leading platform in the emerging field of digital psychiatry. This article synthesizes the author's earlier pilot work and publicly available technical documentation; it does not report new empirical data.

title: High-Assurance Bot Detection on Steam: A Hybrid Ensemble Learning Framework for Detecting Automated Steam Accounts Using Profile Metadata
authors: Eoin Smylie; Sandeep Shiraskar; Hossein Beyzavi; Arohi Shiraskar; Abeer Albluwi; Maram Albalawi; Georges Nehmetallah; Frederic Rizk; Patrick Rizk; Rodrigue Rizk; K Kesharwani Santosh; Dominick Rizk
abstract: The proliferation of automated accounts ("bots") on the Steam gaming platform poses significant security and economic risks, ranging from phishing scams to the manipulation of in-game economies via "farming" botnets. While behavioral analysis of gameplay trajectories exists, it requires computationally expensive, non-public server-side data. This paper presents a lightweight, highly effective machine learning approach to detect Steam bots using only public profile metadata. We curated a novel dataset of 2,289 gold-labeled accounts and engineered features based on profile completeness, naming conventions, and engagement metrics. We evaluated a spectrum of classifiers, ranging from deep neural networks to ensemble methods. Our results demonstrate that while Deep Learning models achieve high performance (AUC 0.992), tree-based ensemble methods specifically Random Forest and Voting Classifiers offer superior robustness for this tabular data. By optimizing for recall to minimize security risks, our proposed ensemble approach achieved 95.63% accuracy and 100% recall on the test set, proving that metadata analysis is a viable first line of defense against automated gaming accounts.

title: Can Large Language Models Be Trusted for AI-Based Intrusion Detection in Cybersecurity? An Evidence-Grounded Log Analysis
authors: Hossein Beyzavi; Sandeep Shiraskar; Abeer Albluwi; Maram Albalawi; Dominick Rizk; Frederic Rizk; Patrick Rizk; Georges Nehmetallah; Rodrigue Rizk; K Kesharwani Santosh
abstract: Security Operations Centers (SOCs) rely heavily on system logs for intrusion detection, yet the growing volume and complexity of modern infrastructure logs make manual analysis increasingly impractical. While traditional intrusion detection systems provide automated alerts, they often lack contextual reasoning and interpretable explanations. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) offer new opportunities for semantic log analysis and natural-language reasoning, motivating their use as automated SOC assistants. However, existing studies largely evaluate LLMs based on detection performance or qualitative usefulness, without rigorously assessing whether their explanations are grounded in actual log evidence. In this paper, we propose a systematic evaluation framework for applying closed-weight, web-accessible LLMs to intrusion detection from raw Linux system logs. Using standardized prompts and fixed log windows, we treat each LLM as a black-box SOC analyst that produces structured intrusion assessments, suspicion scores, and cited evidence. Beyond traditional labels, we introduce evidence faithfulness as a core evaluation metric, measuring whether the evidence referenced by a model is explicitly present in the input logs. We evaluate multiple widely used closed weight online LLMs, including ChatGPT, Gemini, Grok, NotebookLM, Perplexity, and Claude. Our results reveal significant differences in suspicion calibration, alert generation, and evidence grounding across models. While several LLMs consistently flag suspicious activity, unfaithful or partially hallucinated evidence remains common. These findings highlight that reliable explanation grounding is essential for trustworthy LLM-assisted intrusion detection and motivate future research on evaluation-driven prompt and model design.

title: Appearance-Based Cyberbullying Detection in Dialectal Arabic: A New Gulf Body-Shaming Benchmark and MARBERTv2-based Classification Framework
authors: Abeer Albluwi; Maram Albalawi; Sandeep Shiraskar; Arohi Shiraskar; Hossein Beyzavi; Georges Nehmetallah; Frederic Rizk; Patrick Rizk; Rodrigue Rizk; K Kesharwani Santosh; Dominick Rizk
abstract: Cyberbullying on visual-based social platforms is a growing online safety risk, particularly for young women and adolescents. Appearance-targeted harassment, specifically body-shaming, induces severe psychological harm but remains understudied in the Arabic-speaking world. Existing Arabic cyberbullying research focuses primarily on general offensive language and largely employs Twitter corpora, overlooking culturally and linguistically nuanced body-shaming expressions in Gulf and wider dialectal Arabic. To address this gap, this paper introduces the first Arabic Gulf body-shaming dataset, comprising 14,716 comments collected from TikTok and Instagram and annotated into three categories: non-bullying (NBS), general bullying (B), and explicit body-shaming (BS). We present a transformer-based classification framework by fine-tuning MARBERTv2, a state-of-the-art Arabic language model, for robust detection of appearance-focused harms. Experimental results show that our method achieves 91.02% accuracy and 0.9093 macro F1, outperforming all baseline systems. The dataset and findings provide a foundational benchmark for future research and support emerging digital-safety initiatives across the Gulf region.

title: The Role of Family Awareness in Reducing Information Crimes: A Descriptive Analytical Study on A Sample of Saudi families in Al-Qunfudhah Governorate
authors: Muzinah Alsayed; Basma Alsinari
abstract: The study aimed to identify the role of family awareness in reducing information crimes from the point of view of a sample of Saudi families in Al-Qunfudhah Governorate, as well as identifying the forms of information crimes, and their most important risks, and determining the role of the family in developing awareness among its members of information crimes, and knowing the societal obstacles that limit Developing family awareness of information crimes, and the study relied on the social survey approach as an appropriate method for the study. The results of the study are that the most important form of information crime from the point of view of Saudi families in Al-Qunfudhah is the robbery of bank credit cards with a rate of (68%), and that the most important risk of information crime is exploitation and extortion of the victim to obtain her money with a rate of (90.7%), and that the most important role of the family is in developing awareness Its members have awareness of information crimes within the family by dealing with caution with internet and social networking sites by (98%). 88.3%. The study recommended the need to train Saudi family members to take the necessary security measures, procedures, and precautions to protect themselves and their families from information crimes and reduce their risks, which may be due to poor family awareness of these crimes.

title: Re-Distill: A Multi-Stage Retrieval Framework for Functional–Non-Functional Requirement Linking in Software Engineering
authors: Ashwag Almohammady; Reem Alnanih; Nahed Alowidi
abstract: Non-functional requirements (NFRs) are critical for ensuring software quality, yet they remain difficult to identify due to their implicit and loosely defined relationship with functional requirements (FRs). Existing research predominantly focuses on NFR classification, leaving the more practical problem of linking FRs with their corresponding NFRs largely underexplored. To bridge this gap, this research introduces Re-Distill, a framework that treats FR–NFR association as a retrieval task. It adopts a curriculum-guided, data-centric distillation strategy to improve semantic representations and capture the interdependencies between FRs and NFRs. The framework combines general semantic adaptation, domain-specific specialization, and teacher-guided hard-negative mining in a contrastive learning setting. During inference, it integrates dense and lexical retrieval with cross-encoder reranking to produce ranked NFR candidates for unseen FR queries. Experiments on an expanded FR–NFR dataset show consistent improvements throughout all training stages. The resulting model achieves a Recall@10 of 70.79%, significantly outperforming the zero-shot baseline (42.36% Recall@10). These results highlight the effectiveness of retrieval-based approaches for functional–non-functional requirement linking, providing a practical and scalable way to undertake software requirement analysis.

title: Inference limits in partially observable Ethereum blockchains
authors: Muhammad Arshad; Ali Algrani
abstract: While full ledger access is theoretically possible on public blockchains, in reality it is often not possible. Things that can be seen are limited by storage limitations, client design, indexing services, and off-chain execution pathways. This means that entire ledger objects are rarely used for empirical blockchain analysis; instead, observable projections are typically used. In this research, the observability of blockchain is recast as an inferential problem with incomplete observation. Studying identifiability, information loss, and irreducible uncertainty under coarsened access, the framework defines a full ledger, an observable ledger, and an observability mechanism. Three distinct visibility regimes, independent Bernoulli, clustered, and activity-dependent, are assessed in the simulation study. Reduced visibility raises uncertainty inflation, root mean squared error, variance, and mean squared error across all three regimes. The most severe deterioration happens when the condition of the underlying ledger determines visibility. This empirical study employs Google BigQuery's publicly indexed Ethereum block data spanning blocks 18,000,000 to 18,001,000. Over the chosen Ethereum period, descriptive summaries reveal a large amount of fluctuation in gas utilised, transaction count, and basic charge per gas at the block level. Experiments with controlled missingness on the observed slice reveal that RMSE and trend estimate bias grow with increasing missingness, and that the degree of distortion is significantly affected by whether the incompleteness is MCAR-like, MAR-like, or MNAR-like. This research proves that partial observability isn't just a secondary data issue; it can significantly affect inference on Ethereum block-level summaries.

title: Domain-Adaptive Sentiment and Topic Analysis Using LLMs in Low-Resource Language: A Case Study on Turkish Airport Reviews
authors: Ali Görgülü; Huseyin Ozgur Kamali; Zulal Oz; Gorkem Mert; Rukiye Savran Kızıltepe; Murat Karakuş; Arwa Basbrain
abstract: The exponential growth of Natural Language Processing (NLP) has transformed the analysis of digital feedback, yet a significant disparity remains for low-resource, morphologically rich languages such as Turkish, particularly within domains such as the civil aviation industry. This study addresses the aforementioned gap by establishing a robust and domain-adaptive framework for sentiment analysis (SA) and topic classification using Turkish reviews for the most visited 9 airports in Türkiye.We have constructed a high-quality corpus derived from 8,372 Turkish reviews across major airports in Türkiye, employing proprietary Large Language Models (LLMs), namely GPT(gpt-4o-mini), Gemini(gemini-2.5-flash-lite), and Claude(claude-3-haiku), to generate distinct labels with verified reliability. To mitigate the computational limitations of full model training, we utilize Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) strategies, specifically Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), to adapt 5 open-source base models: BERTurk, XLM-RoBERTa, Llama 3.2, Qwen 2.5, and Gemma 2. We conduct a comprehensive evaluation across 151 fine-tuned model configurations-93 for SA and 58 for topic classification-to investigate the combined effects of input granularity (review vs. sentence level) alongside assessments of temporal, cross-airport, and out-of-domain generalization. Furthermore, we explore pipeline optimizations through loss function and preprocessing (Raw, Preprocessed and Mixed) strategy ablations, supported by detailed computational cost and qualitative error analyses. The results indicate that the fine-tuned models outperform their zero-shot counterparts, particularly in topic classification, where generic models failed to capture latent themes effectively. While the best zero-shot baseline(orpogemma-2-9b-tr)achieved an F1-Score of only 0.6037 ± 0.0108, our fine-tuned model(llama_3.2_3b)reached an F1-Score of 0.8228±0.0056 in topic classification, representing an absolute F1-Score improvement of 0.2191. In SA, domain adaptation proved similarly valuable, elevating the base model’s(llama_3.2_3b_base)F1-Score from 0.5299±0.0099 to 0.9156±0.0042(llama_3.2_3b). Furthermore, our analysis reveals that processing feedback at the review level yields superior predictive performance (achieving an F1-Score of 0.9156 ± 0.0042 byllama_3.2_3b) compared to sentence-level granularity (achieving an F1-Score of 0.8998±0.0048 byllama_3.2_3b) in SA, underscoring the importance of contextual integrity in agglutinative languages. In the out-domain generalization tests on unseen future reviews,llama_3.2_3breached an F1-Score of 0.9361 in SA and 0.7367 in topic classification.

title: Ontology‐Enhanced Deep Learning for Mechanistic Prediction of Drug–Drug Interactions: A Clinically Interpretable Framework
authors: Adeeb Noor
abstract: Drug-drug interactions (DDIs) have critical impacts on patient safety and healthcare efficiency because of their significant contributions to adverse drug reactions. Accurately predicting DDIs and their biological mechanisms is therefore essential, yet remains challenging. This study aims to enhance prediction accuracy and mechanistic interpretability by leveraging biomedical ontologies. We developed ontology-based embeddings from SIDER, DrugBank, and Gene Ontology data to represent phenotypic, functional, and mechanistic drug characteristics, providing biologically enriched features for neural network-based prediction of DDIs. The proposed framework achieved robust performance, validated externally (receiver operating characteristic area under the curve values up to 0.94), and effectively predicted DDIs across 11 pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic mechanisms. These mechanism-specific predictions emphasize the biological and pharmacological relevance of putative DDIs, enhancing interpretability by identifying high-risk DDI mechanisms linked to known adverse reactions. Our approach, integrating ontology-based embeddings with deep learning, therefore not only significantly improves DDI prediction but also supports clinical decisions to mitigate adverse drug reactions risks, albeit indirectly.
